quest.title: Give Her Sweetness
quest.description: Some would seek to cause trouble during the festival. They cannot be allowed to ruin this surprise...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Festive Fervor x80, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4

chapter.num: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Second Gift
chapter.title: Give Her Sweetness

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace, you're here! Have you seen Dori?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: She just left. I got here early, and she had already started doing business, so we wrapped things up right away.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: She left the city as soon as I handed her the travel permit and tax waiver I promised.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, she sure didn't waste any time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, how'd it go? Did she tell you where the gem came from?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes. According to the local gem merchants, the ore was retrieved from a nameless ruin in the desert several months ago. The ruin is in very poor condition. Even the writing on the walls is nearly impossible to read.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Dori mentioned something even more concerning, though. Apparently, the craftsman made another gem just like this one.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, there's two?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes. The ore had a crack down the middle. The craftsman believed it would be impossible to repair, so they turned it into two gems instead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, where's the other gem now?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That's exactly what I'd like to know. If this gem truly provides the power of foresight, the consequences could be detrimental in the wrong hands.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Funny enough, I heard a caravan was robbed just this morning, in a remote part of the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You think it's related to the other gem?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I can't say for sure, but I do know this... Only small-scale caravans or ones carrying important goods travel on remote paths like that, and their routes are highly confidential...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: It's certainly possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like we need to investigate the site of the robbery... But, what about the preparations for the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Dehya said we can meet up with everyone later. If we hurry, we should be able to get back in time.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Of course, if you have other plans, please don't feel obliged to come with me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, we're in this together! There's no way we're backing out now!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's head out!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I should've known you would say that. Thank you for all your help.

choices.text: Whoever attacked the caravan was able to "predict" its exact location.

talks.objective: Go to the scene of the crime

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I believe the robbery took place not too far from here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, we really are in the middle of nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, over here.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Do you sense that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I sense a trace amount of elemental energy.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Exactly. Many among the desert tribes are capable of wielding elemental energy. The same is true for the Eremites. Some use that power to attack caravans and earn some quick Mora.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, are those... broken planks over there?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes. All that's left of the transport wagon, I would imagine. Strange... the wood looks charred. Was there an explosion?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I see traces of activity over there. Let's follow the road and see what we can find.

talks.objective: Ask the caravan about the situation

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: *sigh* I can't believe this. We made sure to pick a remote path, and we still got ambushed...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Excuse me, sorry for the interruption...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Ahhh...! Who's there?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm Candace, the guardian of Aaru Village. I'm trying to learn more about the robbery that took place this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: G—Guardian!?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Calm down, I think we're safe. Pretty sure stealing's not in a guardian's job description.

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: Oh, yeah... right...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Don't mind him. Some of our guys are still on edge after the robbery this morning...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I can sympathize, of course. There's no need to be nervous. Although... is this where you plan to set up camp? Caravan Ribat isn't far, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: *sigh* The robbery took everything from us. We can't just let that slide. So, I'm taking my men to confront them, and get back some of what they stole, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I would caution against that, especially when it looks like you're low on rations as it is. In the desert, impulsivity and overconfidence can be fatal.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: What was it that you were transporting?

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: Hazardous materials.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Excuse me?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: For the love of... You can't just say that! Listen, it was just some firecrackers and fireworks, that's all!

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: But, that's what the crates had written on them...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: They're fireworks. What else would they be labeled as? "Perishable goods"?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: *sigh* Just... ignore him, please. As you can see, some of my guys aren't particularly bright. If the guards at Caravan Ribat hear of this, we'll get questioned all over again...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So the charred marks on the planks... are from the fireworks?)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: And where were you sending those goods?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: To some tribal camps in the desert. Everybody's looking to celebrate with the Sabzeruz Festival coming up.

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Even small businesses like us got a share of the orders, mostly the long-distance transports that no one else wanted.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I see... Could you describe the robbery to us?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Well, it was like this... We had just set out on the remote path when—

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: A web of thorns and vines suddenly blocked our way!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vines?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: What? No, why would there be vines in the desert? Our wagon got stuck in the sand, that's what happened. I'm sure it was a trap!

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: After that—

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: Bombs started falling from the sky!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bombs?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Just... stop talking. That robbery messed you up more than I thought.

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Don't listen to his nonsense. He's just a bit... shaken up by what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Anyway, as we were trapped, the bandits started firing rockets at us, which made a lot of the fireworks go off. In the middle of all the chaos, they ran off with the rest of our stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Did you see what they looked like?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Ah, no... we couldn't really see anything. There was sand everywhere, and we were more preoccupied with getting out alive...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Although, I did notice that one of the bandits had this green stone...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Did it look anything like this?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Yes! Exactly like that! I just couldn't make sense of it... If you already have something that valuable, why go after our cheap firecrackers?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Unless the "hazardous materials" were targeted for some other reason...)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Alright, I think I understand the situation. Thank you for your cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I would still urge you to head to Caravan Ribat and report the incident. For your own safety, don't let your anger lead you to do something foolish.

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: Well... alright. We'll just take another quick break before we head over...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Good. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #Alright, we should be out of ear-shot. So... what do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Yes, I feel the same way. Their leader was clearly hiding something. I think we can safely say those weren't simple firework shipments.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: And now, whatever "hazardous materials" they were transporting have fallen into the hands of another group of bandits.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So one group of bad guys attacked the other...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: It's very possible. In any case, our biggest concern right now is the group that currently has the goods, and what their goal may be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The Sabzeruz Festival is coming up...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I see what you mean. Their methods were precise and effective. It's very likely they're exploiting the visions granted by the gem.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: The situation could be even more precarious than we thought. Mmm... I don't think we should hide this any longer. Let's head back to Caravan Ribat and explain the situation to the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Rest here for now, you two. I'll be back as soon as I've spoken to the guards.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon hopes the Sabzeruz Festival doesn't get ruined. Things are turning out to be more complicated than we expected...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh? And what "things" would those be? Sounds like something the General Mahamatra should know about.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Cyno! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm here on business, investigating an unusual robbery case.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, could it be the same one we've been investigating!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds like you've been hard at work.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Just doing my duty. By the way, I brought something that I think might help with the investigation. Here, have some Padisarah Pudding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... okay! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Well, find any clues? They say the "proof is in the pudding," after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *coughing*...! Did you have to tell that joke when Paimon had a mouthful of pudding! She almost choked...

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Anyway, back to the matter at hand. Tell me about this robbery case of yours.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...I see, so you and Candace already did a preliminary investigation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Candace can tell you the rest when she gets back. That merchant group was really suspicious!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Alright, you can leave the rest to me.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: On a different note, do you have any other plans for the day?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we'll probably head back with Candace! We're meeting up with everyone to prepare for the su—

response.speaker: Player
response.text: P—Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Su—... Super awesome dinner we're planning tonight!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Cyno's working quarters aren't too far from Nahida's... Did Tighnari tell him about the surprise?)

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: ...Strange. Sounds like you're hiding something from me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? N—No, not at all! We'd never do anything like that!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Do you know why Henna Berries can't tell a lie?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Wh—Why?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Because... they're always going to be "read" straight through.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Get it? Like the color... I can explain it if you need.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We get it! We get it!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: S—Seriously! There's no secret!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Is that so? You're not afraid of ending up like the bass in the lake?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What...?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Because, they always wind up eating their "worms."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't do this anymore...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Who knew being interrogated by the General Mahamatra was this miserable...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Hmm? Someone's being interrogated? Did I miss something?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Candace! Thank goodness you're back! Please save us!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: What happened? Can't be anything too bad, if Cyno's grinning from ear to ear.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Nice to see you, Candace.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: #{NICKNAME} already updated me on everything, so you can leave the robbery case to me.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: But, when I asked about their plans this afternoon, they started dodging my questions.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: This afternoon... Aren't we heading back to Port Ormos to work on the "surprise"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C—Candace! It... It's supposed to be a secret!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: It's alright. Cyno has always been part of the plan.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Why didn't you say something sooner!?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Well, once you told me about the case, I realized I might not make it this afternoon. I was going to ask you to tell the group, but you decided to end the conversation.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seriously!? So, we had to listen to a couple of Cyno jokes for nothing?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was three jokes, actually...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Right, we never told you who was involved... Apologies. That was our mistake.

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Well, with that resolved, could you tell the group I've got a case?

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: Oh, and these are the items I was supposed to get. Could you take them back with you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! We've got this!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: I would hope so. I just handed it to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Enough already!

response.speaker: Cyno
response.text: You think so? Then, tell me your secret!

choices.text: Don't tell me you did all that just to make a joke...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... We're back. Finally free from all those terrible jokes...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Haha, I rarely get to spend time with Cyno outside of work. I'm sure he's just happy you came back for the Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That explains why he had all those jokes ready to go, even while on the job... Paimon will never understand how he doesn't give himself a cringe attack...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah...! Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace? Did you have another vision?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes... I saw... two people enter the alley over there...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: They seemed suspicious... I think they were talking about something dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dangerous!? Maybe they're the bandits from earlier!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you see what they looked like?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: No... Unfortunately, the visions are very blurry. I could only catch a few words and some vague images...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, let's sneak up on them! If they're the ones looking to cause trouble during the Sabzeruz Festival, we should catch them in the act!
...know nothing...
...secret signal...
...explosion goes off...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, did you hear that? Sounds like they're talking about something dangerous...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Let's try to get closer.
...when... passes by on the Flower Carriage... we'll launch it...
...factor in the object's trajectory...
...completely foolproof.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Stop your planning at once!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Huh? I—Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, it's you two? What kind of terrible plan were you talking about just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something about explosions, and the Flower Carriage...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The connections we make reveal a lot about the mind. The fact that you went to a dark place simply shows the way you think.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Honestly, Paimon, what did you think we were doing? We were just discussing the birthday surprise.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Like I said, that's not it! We have more than just a heartless, transactional relationship... You're overthinking the whole thing!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It was your theory in the first place... that Mehrak disappeared after working for you all this time without anything in return.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I think I'm allowed some dramatics! Mehrak hasn't come back since I sent it out for coffee!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Perhaps seeing the underlings at the Akademiya pick up coffee for their seniors taught Mehrak something about its own situation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You're saying I treat Mehrak like my inferior? I would never! I'm just worried Mehrak had some sort of awful experience and decided to run away.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Maybe something triggered an existential crisis, and Mehrak became so angry about its mechanical existence... it decided to never come back!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's certainly an... imaginative conclusion.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: No, that's impossible... I created Mehrak myself, and I perform regular maintenance every week. There's no way Mehrak would be that heartless...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And here you are in Port Ormos, telling me all this when I'm supposed to be working.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's good I ran into you, actually. I was hoping you could take a look at my proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Huh, I thought you were confident in your abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: It's not like that! I just wanted to confirm the route for the Flower Carriage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, I know nothing about the route for the Flower Carriage.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: What? You're not involved in the Festival at all? The Akademiya couldn't convince you to help out?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Organizing festivals is not part of my job description. You really think the Akademiya could convince me otherwise?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You've got a point... Well, could you at least take a look at the final explosion?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Explosion?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yep. The candy tower I designed is going to hit the Flower Carriage at a designated time and explode into pieces, shooting candy in all directions.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Not the dangerous kind of explosion, though. It's supposed to look like fireworks.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: I consulted a bunch of food engineering papers, so it's completely safe. The candy is soft, and the packaging is as smooth as Silk Flower fabric.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Once I receive the secret signal, Mehrak will activate the mechanism from afar. That way, I can make sure the explosion goes off at the right time and place.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And when is that supposed to be?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: When the Dendro Archon passes by on the Flower Carriage. Once we receive the signal, we'll launch it, and... KABOOM!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Don't forget to factor in the object's trajectory and the humidity level.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Already done! The mechanism inside the candy tower controls for those factors. The plan is completely foolproof.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... So that's what all this was about...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You had your mind set on a very different interpretation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, well... about that...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's alright. Let me explain.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The ability to see the future? That's incredible...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You formulated a hypothesis based on your interpretation of the gem's abilities, yet the results fail to corroborate it.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Perhaps this calls for a different postulation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, maybe you could dumb that down a little?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You assumed you were seeing the future. But, what if you were actually seeing the past?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The past?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Jahangir said this was the second time his wind generator broke down. Mechanical failures of that nature come with predictable consequences. His lack of surprise suggests something similar happened in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: As for the falling crates... During a busy time like the Sabzeruz Festival, people often stack their crates on both sides of the street, likely leading to similar accidents.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Seeing people have a private conversation in a secluded place is even more common.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: So, you're saying... we just happened to witness events that have occurred before?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It's easy for mundane events to appear special.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: So, either you can predict the future and make it deviate off course, or you happened to witness the past... Yeah, the second option seems a bit easier to swallow.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: That's not why I brought it up. I was simply trying to offer a change in perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it does explain what we saw...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The conditions and actions required to trigger this power are still unclear. If you plan to investigate further, you should pay attention to those two factors.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Speaking of a change in perspective... Maybe YOU were the one that scared Mehrak off!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: An ingenious thought... if Mehrak and I had never met before.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yeah, Mehrak should be used to you, especially after I programmed it to recognize your voice... Something else must have happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kaveh, if Mehrak is missing, what's that thing coming towards us right now?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hm? Mehrak!? Where have you been!?

dialogues.speaker: Mehrak
dialogues.text: Beep-beep.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You went to look for more coffee beans because the shop was out of stock? Hey, if they're out, they're out. You don't have to go that far...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Mehrak sure is persistent...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace? Something on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I was just thinking about Mr. Alhaitham's theory. It makes sense, until we factor in the robbery in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, you're all here. Something wrong? You look troubled...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Just trying to work through some mysteries... Oh, right! It's almost time for our meeting. We'll catch you up on the way.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm needed at the House of Daena. See you later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Bye-bye!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: If you don't know what to say, then don't say anything at all! You have to stop interrupting me!

dialogues.speaker: Hizir
dialogues.text: But, I was just telling the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Yakup
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're hopeless...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Nice of you to finally show up! All young and capable, and yet not one of you could get here before a senior such as myself.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Apologies, Madame Faruzan. We, uh, got caught up in a discussion...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: A discussion more important than the candy tower? Finding a suitable material for the candy — that was supposed to be the priority, or we might not make it in time for the Parade.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well? Did you figure something out?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Yes. Took me several dozen papers, but I got it in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, at least you young people work fast... Alright, now's no time to slack off. We need to focus, or we still might not make it in time.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: You're right... We should leave the other case to Cyno. There's not much we can do from here, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Well, then let's get to it — don't make me order you around like little kids.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh, and Kaveh... You wanted a mechanism to simulate the Parade, right? I finished it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Already!? That's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Hmph! No more difficult than Haravatat's standard curriculum a hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Here, let me know if it works.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Thank you so much, Madame Faruzan!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, mind helping me test this out? I need to observe the Carriage to make adjustments to the candy tower.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure, just leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Alright, now it's time for the production phase. Go ahead and sketch out the design — we'll deal with the candy part.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Where are Collei and Dehya?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: They've been at Miss Dunyarzad's house the past couple of days, working on the candy decorations. I'm sure they have it under control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, now that you mention it... Why aren't we meeting in the city? Wouldn't that be more convenient?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Because we'd be right under the Dendro Archon's nose. It would be too easy to run into her.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Being further away from Sumeru City means our chances of getting caught are lower.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: The last thing we want is for the Dendro Archon to discover the surprise...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Huh? What's going on here? I thought I just heard my name.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: ...K—K—Kaveh!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: M—Madam Faruzan?

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: You call this a design! What possessed you to use that kind of material for the roof!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, um... I...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: (Play along!)

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: This design overturns centuries of Sumeru architectural tradition! The Dendro Archon would be devastated if she saw it.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Yes! You're right. I mean, just look at the... the facade! Completely unacceptable, haha...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: I'm sure you can come up with a new design in a few days, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Of course! I'll get something to you first thing tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Oh, so it was a conversation about architecture. Hmm... I think innovation can be a good thing.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Don't mind us, Archon. Kaveh is an intelligent young man. He just goes overboard sometimes. Really lets his imagination run wild... Don't worry. It's a simple fix.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I see...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Alright, if you say so...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Still, I'd be happy to take a look at the plans. I might be able to give some pointers.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, is this not a good time?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Um, well... about that...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (They all look extremely uncomfortable... Are they afraid to show me their work? Or embarrassed to talk about the problem?)

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: The plans... Oh, I almost forgot! My friend has them! That guy's always causing trouble, hahaha... I'll fetch them in a bit.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: (Hmm... They're definitely up to something.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...! Nilou!)

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: ...Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Save us! Noooooow!)

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Archon!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, Nilou! Did you need something?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yes! I've been looking for you all over! The folks at Zubayr Theater had some questions about the program for the Sabzeruz Festival.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, then I'll head over right away. Thank you for coming all this way, Nilou.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: No, thank YOU for taking time out of your busy schedule to pay us a visit!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's no trouble! I've had a lot of free time lately. I heard things were getting lively at Port Ormos, so I decided to come take a look.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, I guess we should head back, Nilou. See you all some other time.

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Phew...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That... That was too close...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Sorry for yelling just now, Kaveh. Don't worry — I have nothing but absolute confidence in your design.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I don't make a habit of speaking like that to a capable junior.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: It's alright. I understand...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, Kaveh! By the way...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: AHEM! Hop to it, Kaveh! We need those plans! Do I really need to watch you do the revisions for this to get done!?

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: ...I'm going, I'm going!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Oh, uh... I just wanted to say, you can always come to me if you ever need guidance or help with anything.

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Don't worry, Archon! This is all under control!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Take care, Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh... Paimon's heart can't take much more of this...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Let's move our meeting spot to Pardis Dhyai, just in case. Port Ormos was a good choice in terms of location, but we forgot to factor in the festivities...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Should we go now?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: I think that's the best choice. Kaveh can focus on designing the candy tower. The rest of us will transport the materials.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Don't worry, Kaveh. I'll support you no matter what design you come up with!

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: Thanks...

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: (Madame Faruzan said she doesn't normally yell at her juniors, but I feel like I just got a glimpse of a true senior researcher...)

response.speaker: Kaveh
response.text: (Even though there's nothing "senior" about her appearance...)

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Alright, it's decided. Let's meet tomorrow at Pardis Dhyai.

choices.text: He'll revise the design right away...

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh! Not bad. Looks like a successful simulation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Thanks to you two, I already have a pretty good idea of how the tower should look.

dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: If this was the actual Carriage, the Dendro Archon would have been thrown off by now...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Um, well... the simulation was a little questionable, but I still managed to come up with a few ideas for the tower.

dialogues.speaker: Aruj
dialogues.text: Ugh... my leg...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The traces are pointing this way...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Let's go up.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Looks like something left behind by the caravan...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: These too...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Shouldn't be far now...
